title: IS-GPS-200N: NAVSTAR GPS Space Segment / Navigation User Segment Interfaces
summary: The master interface specification for the legacy GPS L1 C/A and L2C (and P(Y) at the public level) signals: code generation, signal structure, and the full LNAV/CNAV navigation message bit layouts. Every GPS receiver, simulator and spoofing detector ultimately decodes against this document.
key_takeaways: Defines LNAV subframe and CNAV message formats bit-for-bit
Ephemeris, clock and ionosphere parameter algorithms live here
Revisions are managed through the public ICWG process

title: IS-GPS-705J: NAVSTAR GPS Space Segment / User Segment L5 Interfaces
summary: Interface specification for the GPS L5 safety-of-life band signal: I5/Q5 codes, the L5 CNAV message, and signal characteristics. L5's higher chipping rate and wider band make it more robust to narrowband interference than L1 C/A.
key_takeaways: Defines the L5 dataless pilot (Q5) and data (I5) channels
CNAV message types shared with L2C
Draft uprevisions were discussed at the 2025 public ICWG

title: IS-GPS-800J: NAVSTAR GPS Space Segment / User Segment L1C Interfaces
summary: Interface specification for the modernized L1C civil signal designed for interoperability with Galileo E1 and other GNSS: BOC/TMBOC modulation, Weil-code ranging codes, and the CNAV-2 message.
key_takeaways: L1C uses a pilot plus data component, like Galileo E1
CNAV-2 adds FEC-coded subframes
Key reference for multi-GNSS L1 receiver design

title: GPS Interface Control Documents (ICWG index)
summary: Index page for the public GPS ICDs and ISs (200, 705, 800, 870 etc.), change notices and public ICWG meeting material. Useful to find the current revision and pending changes such as integrity support message formats.
key_takeaways: Single place to check which revision is in force
Hosts proposed change notices and meeting redlines

title: GPS Standard Positioning Service (SPS) Performance Standard, 5th Edition
summary: The formal commitment the US government makes about civil GPS signal-in-space accuracy, availability, continuity and integrity. It is the baseline to compare against when judging whether a receiver anomaly is the signal or interference.
key_takeaways: States guaranteed SIS user range error and availability levels
Defines what counts as a major service failure
Basis for RAIM and integrity assumptions in aviation

title: Galileo Open Service Signal-In-Space Interface Control Document (OS SIS ICD) Issue 2.1
summary: Specification of the Galileo open service signals (E1, E5a, E5b, E6 at the structure level) and the F/NAV and I/NAV navigation messages. Needed for any multi-constellation receiver or Galileo decoder.
key_takeaways: Defines I/NAV and F/NAV page layouts
Ranging code and modulation details for E1 and E5
Newer issues are listed in the GSC reference documents library

title: Galileo OSNMA Signal-In-Space Interface Control Document Issue 1.1
summary: Defines Open Service Navigation Message Authentication: how TESLA-chain MACs and keys are embedded in spare I/NAV bits so a receiver can cryptographically verify that navigation data came from Galileo. It is the first civil GNSS data-authentication service in operation.
key_takeaways: Uses a TESLA key chain with delayed key disclosure
Authenticates navigation data, not the ranging signal itself
Requires loose time sync and a public key obtained out of band

title: Galileo OSNMA Receiver Guidelines Issue 1.3
summary: Companion to the OSNMA ICD describing how a receiver should process OSNMA: time-sync requirements, key and Merkle-tree handling, verification procedures and how to report authentication status to the user.
key_takeaways: Spells out the receiver time-sync assumption that OSNMA security depends on
Covers cold start, key renewal and chain transitions
Practical checklist for implementing OSNMA in software

title: Galileo Open Service Navigation Message Authentication (OSNMA) - service page
summary: Official landing page for the OSNMA service with status, public key and Merkle tree downloads, and links to the ICD and guidelines.
key_takeaways: Where to get the current OSNMA public key and Merkle root
Links to service notices and documentation

title: Galileo High Accuracy Service Signal-In-Space ICD (HAS SIS ICD) Issue 1.0
summary: Defines the free Galileo High Accuracy Service: PPP orbit, clock and bias corrections broadcast on E6-B (and via internet), including message structure and Reed-Solomon encoding.
key_takeaways: Free PPP corrections broadcast from the satellites themselves
Enables decimetre-level PPP without a ground subscription
E6-B message decoding details for receiver builders

title: European GNSS Service Centre - Programme Reference Documents
summary: Library of current Galileo ICDs, service definition documents and receiver guidelines (OS, HAS, OSNMA, SAR). Check here for the latest issue numbers before implementing.
key_takeaways: Authoritative versions of all public Galileo specs
Includes service definition documents with committed performance

title: BeiDou Navigation Satellite System Signal-In-Space ICDs (B1I, B3I, B1C, B2a, B2b)
summary: Official English-language ICD library for BeiDou open service signals, including the BDS-3 B1C and B2a signals that are interoperable with GPS L1C/L5 and Galileo E1/E5a, plus PPP-B2b.
key_takeaways: BDS-3 B1C and B2a are designed for multi-GNSS interoperability
PPP-B2b carries free regional precise corrections
The BeiDou site is the official distribution channel

title: QZSS Performance Standards and Interface Specifications (IS-QZSS)
summary: Japan's QZSS interface specifications covering GPS-compatible signals, the L6 CLAS centimetre-level augmentation and MADOCA PPP services.
key_takeaways: QZSS signals are GPS-interoperable and improve urban-canyon availability in Asia-Oceania
CLAS and MADOCA give free precise positioning corrections
Specs are published openly by the Cabinet Office

title: RTCM 10403.x Differential GNSS (DGNSS) Services - Version 3
summary: The paid-access RTCM v3 standard that defines the binary messages used to stream GNSS corrections and observations (legacy RTK 1001-1012, MSM 1-7 per constellation, ephemerides, SSR). Practically every NTRIP caster and RTK base station speaks it.
key_takeaways: MSM messages replaced legacy observation messages and align with RINEX 3
MSM4/MSM7 are the common choices for RTK
Standard itself is purchased; open parsers document much of it

title: Navipedia: RTK Standards
summary: Free encyclopedia overview of the RTCM correction message families and transport (NTRIP) used for real-time kinematic positioning. A good orientation before buying or parsing the RTCM standard.
key_takeaways: Explains the role of RTCM 2.x vs 3.x messages
Covers NTRIP for internet transport

title: NMEA 0183 Interface Standard
summary: The ASCII serial sentence standard (GGA, RMC, GSA, GSV, VTG...) used by nearly all GNSS receivers and marine electronics. The official standard is sold; open references cover the common sentences.
key_takeaways: Talker IDs distinguish GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, BeiDou and multi-GNSS output
Checksummed ASCII over serial, easy to parse and to fake
Still the lowest-common-denominator GNSS output

title: NMEA 2000 Standard (CAN-based marine network)
summary: CAN bus based marine network standard that carries position, heading, AIS and engine data as PGNs between devices. Paid standard; the community has reverse-documented many PGNs.
key_takeaways: PGNs carry GNSS position, COG/SOG, heading and AIS
Plug-and-play backbone on modern vessels
Unauthenticated bus, relevant to maritime spoofing resilience

title: NMEA Revealed (gpsd project)
summary: A free, detailed field-by-field reference to NMEA 0183 sentences as actually emitted by real receivers, including vendor quirks and version differences. The practical substitute for the paywalled standard.
key_takeaways: Documents real-world deviations from the standard
Covers talker IDs for multi-GNSS output
Written by gpsd maintainers who parse these daily

title: MAVLink Developer Guide
summary: Official documentation for the MAVLink micro air vehicle messaging protocol: message definitions, microservices (mission, parameters, camera, FTP), dialects and code generators.
key_takeaways: Lightweight binary protocol between autopilots, GCS and companion computers
Microservices define stateful exchanges like mission upload
Generators produce bindings for C, Python, Rust and more

title: MAVLink Common Message Set (common.xml)
summary: Reference of all messages and commands in the common dialect, including GPS_RAW_INT, GPS_INPUT for injecting external position, ODOMETRY and VISION_POSITION_ESTIMATE for non-GNSS navigation sources.
key_takeaways: GPS_INPUT and VISION_POSITION_ESTIMATE are the hooks for feeding alternative PNT into an autopilot
ODOMETRY carries full pose plus covariance
Enumerations document EKF and GPS fix status flags

title: MAVLink 2 and Message Signing
summary: Describes MAVLink 2 packet signing: a shared-secret SHA-256 based signature and timestamp appended to frames to authenticate the link and resist replay.
key_takeaways: Signing authenticates but does not encrypt traffic
Key distribution is left to the integrator
Relevant for hardening drone C2 links against injection

title: MAVLink Mission Protocol
summary: The microservice used to upload, download and clear waypoint missions, geofences and rally points between a GCS and an autopilot, with its handshake and retry rules.
key_takeaways: Defines MISSION_COUNT / MISSION_ITEM_INT handshake
Same protocol carries geofence and rally point plans

title: Cursor on Target (NDIA briefing)
summary: Briefing introducing the Cursor on Target XML event schema: the minimal event/point/detail model for exchanging what-when-where of tracked entities between C2 systems.
key_takeaways: Base schema is tiny: event, point, detail
Type strings follow a hierarchical a-f-G-... code derived from symbology
Extensibility lives in the detail element

title: TAK Protocol (takproto) - protobuf encoding of CoT
summary: Documentation of the TAK protocol used by ATAK and TAK Server: how CoT events are framed and carried as protocol buffers over mesh (UDP multicast) and streaming (TCP/TLS) transports, alongside legacy XML.
key_takeaways: Explains version negotiation between XML and protobuf CoT
Mesh vs streaming framing headers
Essential to get a custom app talking to ATAK

title: STANAG 4586 - Standard Interfaces of UAV Control System (UCS) for NATO UAV Interoperability
summary: Public overview of NATO's UAS interoperability standard, which defines a core UCS, a vehicle-specific module and five levels of interoperability from receiving payload data up to full flight control including launch and recovery.
key_takeaways: LOI 1-3 cover payload data and control; LOI 4-5 cover flight control
Vehicle Specific Module isolates proprietary air vehicle interfaces
Full text distributed via NATO / national channels

title: NATO Standardization (topic page)
summary: NATO's public explanation of how STANAGs and Allied publications are produced and ratified, and how interoperability standards flow into national forces. Starting point for locating public STANAG/AP summaries.
key_takeaways: STANAGs record national agreement to implement an Allied publication
Most full texts are restricted; summaries and some APs are public

title: NATO Joint Military Symbology (APP-6) - overview
summary: Overview of APP-6, the NATO standard for map symbols of units, equipment and tactical graphics, now at edition E and aligned with the US MIL-STD-2525 family. Explains frames, affiliation colours and the symbol identification code.
key_takeaways: Affiliation (friend/hostile/neutral/unknown) is encoded by frame shape and colour
APP-6 and MIL-STD-2525 share a common symbol code structure
Open renderers implement it for COP displays

title: MIL-STD-2525 Joint Military Symbology - overview
summary: Summary of the US military symbology standard and its revisions (2525B through E), including the SIDC code formats that symbol renderers and CoT type strings map onto.
key_takeaways: 2525D/E moved to a numeric 20/30-digit SIDC
Basis for symbology in TAK and many C2 tools

title: Executive Order 13905: Strengthening National Resilience Through Responsible Use of PNT Services
summary: US executive order that defines 'responsible use of PNT' and tasks Commerce/NIST, DHS and others to produce PNT profiles, identify critical infrastructure dependencies and pilot-test resilience. It is the root of NIST IR 8323 and the DHS conformance framework.
key_takeaways: Treats PNT disruption as a critical infrastructure risk
Directs creation of voluntary PNT profiles
Calls for testing PNT resilience in federal contracts

title: NIST IR 8323r1: Foundational PNT Profile - Applying the Cybersecurity Framework for the Responsible Use of PNT Services
summary: Maps the NIST Cybersecurity Framework functions (identify, protect, detect, respond, recover) onto systems that produce or consume PNT data. A checklist-style profile for building resilient PNT into an architecture.
key_takeaways: Revision 1 supersedes the 2021 original
Organized around CSF functions, applicable to both GNSS and non-GNSS sources
NIST has signalled alignment with CSF 2.0

title: Resilient PNT Conformance Framework (v1.0)
summary: Defines four cumulative resilience levels for PNT user equipment based on prevent, respond and recover behaviours, so buyers and vendors can describe how a receiver behaves under jamming or spoofing.
key_takeaways: Levels escalate from basic recovery to full prevention and response
Scope is PNT-producing equipment, not downstream consumers
A later v2.0 was reported in 2022 with evaluation guidance

title: Resilient PNT Reference Architecture
summary: Companion to the conformance framework describing architectural patterns (source diversity, integrity checking, holdover) that map to its resilience levels.
key_takeaways: Architectural guidance for multi-source PNT
Mapped to conformance framework levels

title: DHS S&T Positioning, Navigation, and Timing Program
summary: Program hub for DHS PNT work: conformance framework, reference architecture, timing guidance and test events for critical infrastructure.
key_takeaways: Links all DHS resilient PNT publications
Shows the civil critical-infrastructure angle of PNT resilience

title: DoD Directive 4650.05: Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT)
summary: DoD policy directive governing the department's PNT enterprise, including the PNT Oversight Council and responsibilities for assured PNT and navigation warfare. Change 3 (2023) updated the oversight structure.
key_takeaways: Establishes the DoD PNT Oversight Council
Assigns responsibilities for PNT and navigation warfare

title: GAO-21-320SP: Defense Navigation Capabilities - DOD Is Developing Positioning, Navigation, and Timing Technologies to Complement GPS
summary: Technology assessment of DoD's alternative PNT efforts (inertial, vision, celestial, magnetic, signals of opportunity, clocks), with maturity status and challenges. A concise government map of the alt-PNT landscape.
key_takeaways: DOD keeps GPS at the core and adds complements
Reviews maturity of many alt-PNT technology families
Flags integration and testing as recurring challenges

title: National Positioning, Navigation, and Timing Resilience R&D Plan
authors: US National Science and Technology Council
summary: Federal R&D plan responding to EO 13905, laying out research priorities for resilient PNT: threat detection, alternative sources, timing distribution and integrity.
key_takeaways: Identifies federal R&D priorities for PNT resilience
Ties research areas back to EO 13905

title: DOT Complementary PNT Action Plan
authors: US Department of Transportation / Volpe Center
summary: US DOT plan to drive adoption of complementary PNT for transportation and critical infrastructure via stakeholder engagement, specifications, field trials and test ranges.
key_takeaways: Five lines of effort starting with engagement and standards
Leads to field testing of commercial CPNT technologies

title: Analyzing a More Resilient National Positioning, Navigation, and Timing Capability (RR-2970)
summary: DHS-sponsored RAND study of civil US PNT dependence that argues GPS is not the only PNT source in practice and that no single system is a perfect backup. It is a deliberately contrarian counterweight to the 'GPS loss is catastrophic' framing.
key_takeaways: Realistic adaptation lowers estimated economic cost of GPS loss
High bar for a large government-funded GPS backup
Recommends modest investment in threat detection

title: Assessing Alternative Positioning, Navigation and Timing Technologies for Potential Deployment in the EU
summary: JRC test campaign at Ispra of commercial alternative PNT systems (terrestrial beacons, LEO, eLoran-like, fibre timing and others) for DG DEFIS. One of the few side-by-side public evaluations of A-PNT products.
key_takeaways: Mature commercial A-PNT already exists for positioning or timing
Recommends a system-of-systems approach
Warns the diverse tests do not allow a fair head-to-head ranking

title: JRC Complementary Position, Navigation and Timing
summary: JRC activity page hosting the A-PNT assessment report with per-vendor appendices and related EU complementary PNT work.
key_takeaways: Official host for the report and vendor appendices

title: International Committee on GNSS (ICG)
authors: UN Office for Outer Space Affairs
summary: UN forum where GNSS providers coordinate compatibility, interoperability and spectrum protection, including interference detection and mitigation work.
key_takeaways: Venue for multi-GNSS interoperability agreements
Hosts work on interference detection and mitigation

title: EASA Safety Information Bulletin 2022-02R4: GNSS Outage and Alterations Leading to Communication / Navigation / Surveillance Degradation
summary: EASA's running bulletin on GNSS jamming and spoofing affecting aviation since February 2022, with recommendations for authorities, ANSPs, operators and manufacturers. Revision 4 is the current issue.
key_takeaways: Spoofing is treated as the harder-to-detect, higher-risk threat
Recommendations are informational, not mandatory
Affected FIRs are tracked on the EASA website

title: EASA and IATA comprehensive plan to mitigate the risks of GNSS interference
summary: Joint plan from a 2025 EASA/IATA workshop covering reporting, prevention and mitigation, infrastructure and airspace management, and coordination for GNSS interference.
key_takeaways: Standard radio calls and NOTAM Q-codes for interference
Tighter controls on jammer sales
Keep a minimum network of conventional navaids as backup

title: FAA GPS/GNSS Interference Reports and Anomaly Reporting
summary: FAA page for reporting and reviewing GPS anomalies and interference events, with links to notices about planned GPS interference testing and operator guidance.
key_takeaways: Where US pilots file post-flight interference reports
Links to GPS test NOTAM information

title: FAA SAFO 24002: Recognizing and Mitigating GPS/GNSS Disruptions
summary: Safety alert for operators describing how jamming and spoofing manifest in the cockpit and what crews should do: revert to conventional procedures, report to ATC, and file written reports.
key_takeaways: Describes cockpit symptoms of jamming vs spoofing
Advises readiness to use conventional navaids
Later FAA guidance revisions followed in 2026

title: ICAO workshop presentation: GNSS Radio Frequency Interference
summary: ICAO panel presentation on GNSS RFI impacts on flight operations and the regulatory response, from the Flight Safety Measures Panel working group.
key_takeaways: Summarizes operational impacts on avionics
Frames the ICAO-level mitigation agenda

title: OPSGROUP GPS Spoofing Workgroup Final Report
summary: Large practitioner-driven report on airliner GPS spoofing, built from crew surveys and incident data, with recommendations to manufacturers, regulators and operators. The best ground-truth account of what spoofing does to real avionics.
key_takeaways: Spoofing can leave systems like terrain warning degraded after GPS returns
Receivers may retain corrupted data after an event
Argues for retaining ground-based navaids

title: SKYbrary: GNSS Jamming and Spoofing
summary: Aviation safety wiki article explaining jamming vs spoofing, their effects on aircraft systems and the regulatory material around them, with links to bulletins and incident reports.
key_takeaways: Plain-language intro to the aviation impact
Links to EASA/FAA/ICAO references

title: DARPA Adaptable Navigation Systems (ANS)
summary: DARPA program page for ANS, which pursued plug-and-play fusion of navigation sensors and signals of opportunity plus better inertial sensors (cold atom) so platforms can navigate without GPS.
key_takeaways: Combined ASPN-style sensor fusion with new IMU technology
Explicit focus on reconfigurable multi-sensor navigation

title: DARPA Seeks PNT Robustness, Flexibility with All Source Positioning and Navigation Program
summary: Trade-press account of DARPA's ASPN program, which aimed at navigation software architectures that fuse any combination of sensors in plug-and-play fashion.
key_takeaways: Phase 1 built algorithms and a software architecture
Phase 2 targeted real-time fusion on SWaP-representative hardware

title: DARPA Robust Optical Clock Network (ROCkN)
summary: Program to field low-SWaP optical atomic clocks with timing holdover beyond GPS satellite clocks, in a portable airborne variant and a transportable land/sea variant, to keep precise time without GNSS.
key_takeaways: Two technical areas: portable and transportable clocks
Two two-year phases from physics package to operational clock

title: DARPA's ROCkN Program Targets GNSS-Free Precision Timing in Contested Environments
summary: Progress report on ROCkN field tests, including optical clock hardware flown on aircraft and deployed aboard a ship.
key_takeaways: Reports field synchronization and platform trials
Shows optical clocks leaving the lab

title: MagNav Challenge Problem (DAF-MIT AI Accelerator)
summary: Challenge site for airborne magnetic anomaly navigation: compensate the aircraft's own magnetic field out of magnetometer data so the remaining crustal anomaly can be map-matched for GPS-free navigation. Challenge is closed but data and code remain.
key_takeaways: Scored against a professionally compensated tail-stinger magnetometer
Real flight data from survey aircraft
Directly reusable as a hackathon benchmark

title: Signal Enhancement for Magnetic Navigation Challenge Problem
summary: Paper defining the MagNav challenge: the physics of aircraft magnetic interference, the Tolles-Lawson baseline compensation, the dataset, and evaluation, framing it as a physics-informed ML problem.
key_takeaways: Tolles-Lawson is the classical baseline to beat
Scalar magnetometer mixes Earth core, crustal anomaly and aircraft fields
Dataset released on Zenodo

title: MagNav Challenge flight dataset (Zenodo)
summary: Zenodo record holding the MagNav challenge flight data: magnetometer, INS, GPS truth and map data from survey flights.
key_takeaways: HDF5 flight lines with truth position
Paired with MagNav.jl loaders

title: Developing a Series of AI Challenges for the United States Department of the Air Force
summary: Describes the Air Force AI challenge series including MagNav, covering both the compensation stage and a navigation stage that turns cleaned readings into position estimates.
key_takeaways: MagNav split into compensation and navigation sub-challenges
Context on how DAF releases open benchmarks

title: NovAtel GAJT-410ML Anti-Jam Antenna Product Sheet
summary: Datasheet for a compact CRPA anti-jam antenna that combines an antenna array and null-forming electronics for land vehicles and small platforms, protecting GPS and Galileo bands and supporting M-code.
key_takeaways: Null-steering CRPA as a drop-in in front of an existing receiver
Shows typical number of nulls and suppression claims for this class

title: NovAtel GAJT-710ML anti-jam antenna
summary: Product page for the larger 7-element GAJT CRPA unit in a hardened enclosure for land vehicles and fixed sites.
key_takeaways: More elements give more simultaneous nulls
Typical military vehicle CRPA form factor

title: Septentrio AIM+ GNSS jamming and spoofing protection
summary: Vendor explanation of AIM+ interference monitoring and mitigation: narrowband and wideband (chirp) jamming suppression in the receiver's signal processing plus layered spoofing detection including Galileo OSNMA.
key_takeaways: Single-antenna, in-receiver mitigation rather than CRPA
Tiered feature levels
OSNMA is one of the anti-spoofing layers

title: Most resilient GNSS receiver: results from Jammertest in Norway
summary: Vendor write-up of its receivers' behaviour during the Jammertest live jamming and spoofing campaign in Norway. Read as a vendor claim, but useful for the scenario descriptions.
key_takeaways: Describes live jamming and spoofing scenarios
Vendor-authored results, not independent

title: The looming threat of GPS jamming and spoofing (u-blox insights)
summary: u-blox explainer on how jamming and spoofing affect mass-market receivers and which receiver-side defences (multi-band, multi-constellation, signal monitoring) help.
key_takeaways: Spoofing many signals consistently is harder with multi-GNSS
Mass-market receivers expose jamming/spoofing indicators that apps can read

title: White Paper: Protecting GNSS Against Intentional Interference
summary: Open white paper summarizing the threat of jamming and spoofing to civil GNSS and the countermeasure landscape (signal authentication, antenna arrays, consistency checks, regulation).
key_takeaways: Taxonomy of intentional interference
Argues for layered defence and authentication

title: Navipedia - ESA GNSS encyclopedia
summary: ESA's free wiki covering GNSS fundamentals, systems, signals, receivers, augmentation and applications. The fastest authoritative lookup for any GNSS term.
key_takeaways: Peer-reviewed style articles maintained by ESA
Covers GPS, Galileo, GLONASS, BeiDou, SBAS

title: Navipedia: Galileo Open Service Navigation Message Authentication
summary: Navipedia article explaining OSNMA's design and status in plain terms before you tackle the ICD.
key_takeaways: Gentle introduction to TESLA-based navigation message authentication

title: GNSS Data Processing, Vol. I: Fundamentals and Algorithms (ESA TM-23)
authors: J. Sanz Subirana, J.M. Juan Zornoza, M. Hernandez-Pajares (ESA)
summary: Free ESA textbook covering GNSS measurement modelling, SPP, differential positioning and PPP algorithms with full equations. Pairs with the gLAB tool.
key_takeaways: Complete measurement model incl. clocks, troposphere, ionosphere
SPP through PPP derivations
Designed to accompany gLAB exercises

title: GNSS Data Processing, Vol. II: Laboratory Exercises (ESA TM-23)
authors: J. Sanz Subirana, J.M. Juan Zornoza, M. Hernandez-Pajares (ESA)
summary: Hands-on lab volume with step-by-step exercises on real data using the gLAB software, from SPP to carrier-phase PPP.
key_takeaways: Ready-made labs usable as a GNSS bootcamp
Real RINEX data throughout

title: A Software-Defined GPS and Galileo Receiver: A Single-Frequency Approach
authors: K. Borre, D. Akos, N. Bertelsen, P. Rinder, S.H. Jensen
summary: Classic textbook that walks through a complete MATLAB GPS software receiver: acquisition, code/carrier tracking, navigation decoding and positioning. The linked University of Colorado page is the official support site for the book's code.
key_takeaways: The canonical entry point to SDR GNSS receivers
MATLAB code makes every loop inspectable
Foundation for many later open SDR receivers

title: Stanford Center for Position, Navigation and Time (SCPNT) / GPS Lab
summary: Home of the Stanford GPS Lab and the annual PNT symposium; hosts papers and presentations on integrity, interference monitoring, spoofing and alternative PNT.
key_takeaways: Annual symposium talks are a good snapshot of the field
Lab papers on aviation integrity and RFI localization

title: Stanford GPS Laboratory
summary: Research group site with publications and theses on GNSS integrity, interference detection and localization, and navigation for aviation.
key_takeaways: Thesis archive is a deep free resource
Publications on GNSS RFI detection and localization

title: Stanford NAV Lab (Grace Gao)
summary: Grace Gao's lab working on robust navigation for autonomous systems: GNSS in urban environments, sensor fusion, integrity and lunar PNT. Course and paper material is linked from here.
key_takeaways: Research on GNSS+vision/lidar fusion and integrity
Home of AA272-related teaching on smartphone GNSS

title: Real-World Spoofing Detection (ION ITM 2025)
authors: Kriezis et al., Stanford GPS Lab
summary: Analyses a real spoofing event in the Mediterranean recorded on low-cost u-blox F9P receivers and evaluates detection approaches on that live data rather than a simulator.
key_takeaways: Real spoofing captured on commodity hardware
Shows which detection cues actually fire in the wild

title: Recent Advances on Jamming and Spoofing Detection in GNSS
summary: Open-access Sensors review of GNSS jamming and spoofing detection methods, finding machine learning is now the dominant approach, and covering combined jamming-plus-spoofing scenarios.
key_takeaways: ML-based detection dominates recent work
Separates jamming-only, spoofing-only and combined attacks

title: Detecting and Mitigating Attacks on GPS Devices
authors: J. Burbank, T. Greene, N. Kaabouch
summary: Open-access review of GPS attack detection and mitigation focused on the GPS-denied case, including the alternative sensors and methods used to keep navigating.
key_takeaways: Covers both detection and what to fall back on
Does not cover timing-only alternatives

title: Overview of satellite navigation spoofing and anti-spoofing techniques
summary: Open-access Frontiers in Physics overview grouping anti-spoofing countermeasures into detection, identification, suppression and localization of the spoofer.
key_takeaways: Four-stage countermeasure taxonomy
Contrasts spoofing with suppression jamming

title: Survey on positioning technology based on signal of opportunity from low earth orbit
summary: Open-access survey of LEO signals-of-opportunity positioning: Doppler methods, error sources, and extracting observables from signals never designed for navigation (unknown codes, poor onboard clocks).
key_takeaways: Doppler positioning is the workhorse for LEO SoOP
Unknown modulation and clock quality are the core difficulties

title: Enter LEO on the GNSS Stage: Navigation with Starlink Satellites
authors: Z. Kassas, M. Neinavaie, et al.
summary: Opportunistic navigation using Starlink downlink signals without cooperation from the operator, describing two ways to extract navigation observables from unknown signals.
key_takeaways: Starlink is usable for navigation without operator support
Signal structure must be partly estimated blind

title: Navigation with Multi-Constellation LEO Satellite Signals of Opportunity: Starlink, OneWeb, Orbcomm, and Iridium
summary: Experimental multi-constellation LEO SoOP navigation combining four commercial constellations, using the simultaneous tracking and navigation (STAN) framework.
key_takeaways: Combining constellations improves geometry and accuracy
STAN estimates satellite states and receiver state together

title: Preliminary Lessons in Conventional Warfighting from Russia's Invasion of Ukraine: February-July 2022
summary: RUSI analysis of the first months of the war, including the scale of Russian electronic warfare and its effect on Ukrainian UAV survival and GNSS-dependent systems.
key_takeaways: EW is a dominant factor in small-UAV attrition
Lessons for resilience of navigation and C2 links

title: Meatgrinder: Russian Tactics in the Second Year of Its Invasion of Ukraine
summary: RUSI report on Russian adaptation in 2023, with a substantial section on electronic warfare density along the front and its impact on drones and GNSS-guided systems.
key_takeaways: Describes dense, layered Russian EW deployment
Drone attrition to EW drives demand for non-GNSS navigation

title: Space Threat Assessment 2025
summary: Annual open-source assessment of counterspace capabilities by country, including electronic counterspace such as GNSS jamming and spoofing.
key_takeaways: Country-by-country counterspace inventory
Tracks GNSS electronic attack incidents year over year

title: Space Threat Assessment 2024
summary: Previous edition of the CSIS counterspace assessment; useful to see how GNSS interference reporting escalated between years.
key_takeaways: Baseline for year-over-year comparison

title: Above Us Only Stars: Exposing GPS Spoofing in Russia and Syria
summary: OSINT investigation that used AIS ship tracks and other data to document systematic Russian GNSS spoofing around sensitive sites and in Syria. A model for detecting spoofing from public tracking data.
key_takeaways: AIS position anomalies reveal spoofing at scale
Methodology is reproducible with public data

title: Researchers home in on origins of Russia's Baltic GPS jamming
summary: Report on Polish research tracing Baltic GNSS jamming to emitters in the Kaliningrad region, with context on the effects on aviation and shipping.
key_takeaways: Emitter localization from distributed measurements
Shows the Baltic as a persistent interference zone

title: GPSJam - daily GPS interference map
summary: Public daily map of likely GPS interference derived from ADS-B navigation accuracy reports broadcast by aircraft. Great for spotting conflict-zone interference and as a data source for hackathon dashboards.
key_takeaways: Derived from ADS-B NIC/NACp degradation
Hex-binned daily snapshots

title: Jammertest - open GNSS jamming and spoofing test event (Andoya, Norway)
authors: Norwegian Communications Authority, FFI, NPRA and partners
summary: Annual open field event where Norwegian agencies transmit real jamming, spoofing and meaconing so vendors and researchers can test PNT equipment. The public test catalogue and community datasets make it the best source of real interference recordings.
key_takeaways: Real over-the-air jamming and spoofing in a controlled area
Published test catalogue and plan
Participants release datasets on GitHub
